# Phase Two — Route-Wide Quality Architecture and Critique

## Five audit architectures

### A — Source grep only
Fast, but cannot prove inherited styling, visibility, mobile geometry, or dynamic content. Rejected as primary evidence.

### B — Screenshot-only visual review
Useful for aesthetics, but weak for hidden overflow, touch target dimensions, and deterministic regression. Rejected as sole gate.

### C — Browser DOM computed-style audit across all twelve routes
Measures the actual rendered mobile surface, can localize defects by route, and can become a durable regression. Chosen.

### D — Rewrite every route proactively
Would create massive unnecessary churn before evidence. Rejected.

### E — Require a class on every text element
Too brittle: many elements are intentionally styled through semantic or ancestor rules. Rejected.

## Chosen quality contract
Use the existing deterministic browser fixture at 390px. Iterate every `RouteModel.ROUTES` destination by hash. Wait for its `[data-panel]` surface to become active, then collect computed evidence from visible descendants.

A defect is objective when one of these occurs:
- document scroll width exceeds viewport width;
- a visible descendant horizontally escapes the viewport beyond a tiny rounding tolerance;
- a visible textual leaf has zero/invisible typography;
- a non-whitespace direct text node sits under a generic unstyled container without a semantic/styled vessel;
- an ordinary visible interactive control collapses beneath a practical mobile touch size without being a compact native exception;
- route panel itself has zero geometry when active.

## Critique improvements
1. Test all twelve routes, not only the four primary dock items.
2. Obtain route IDs from `RouteModel`, not duplicated handwritten names where practical.
3. Keep inspection logic separate from journey orchestration.
4. Exclude script/style/template and hidden descendants.
5. Allow native checkbox/radio controls to remain compact.
6. Allow text links inside deliberately styled navigation/card ancestors while still measuring their geometry.
7. Detect direct text nodes only when meaningful text exists.
8. Treat inherited nontransparent color/font as styled evidence.
9. Report selectors/tag/text snippets for repair localization.
10. Never click destructive or publishing actions.
11. Navigate through hash/location and established route controller.
12. Wait for visible active panel before measuring.
13. Keep global dock/Create visible during every route audit to catch collisions.
14. Recheck document overflow after every route.
15. Add screenshots only for actual failures or representative final state.
16. If defects appear, trace their exact template and CSS owner before source mutation.
17. Use full-file rewrites for every production correction.
18. Keep each test/helper below 120 lines by splitting geometry and route flow.
19. Rerun focused route-wide test first after fixes.
20. Then rerun `npm run test:all` to preserve creation, navigation, privacy, media, and browser behavior.
21. Preserve the user's external-linking exclusion.
22. Do not alter data or publish content.
23. Keep cache generation coherent after any new stylesheet import.
24. Update `REMAINING_WORK` with every real route defect.
25. Close only when the route-wide browser report is clean.

## Architectural boundary
This pass is primarily a verification/discovery pass. Production should change only when the browser names a concrete route defect. The Awtsmoos is not revealed by unnecessary motion; Awtsmoos.com should repair what evidence exposes and leave truthful vessels undisturbed.
